name: Percept: Citizen Ratings of Amsterdam Street Views
description:
Method replication: same categories, category texts and Awful–Great scale as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (new Google Street View views of Amsterdam, © Google). Danish, Labib, Ricker & Helbich (2025, Computers, Environment and Urban Systems 116:102207) built an open-source, smartphone-friendly toolkit that downloads, crops and filters open Mapillary street view images and runs a citizen-science perception survey. In Amsterdam, 331 people gave 22,637 ratings.

What participants do: after consent, they give age (and confirm they are 18+), gender, income, education, postal code and country, as in the app. Then they rate Amsterdam street views from Awful to Great in five blocks of 10 images: walkability, bikeability, pleasantness, greenness and safety. Each block shows the toolkit's own explanation of the category. Images are drawn at random from 71.

Analysis: mean rating per image and category, agreement between raters, correlations between the five categories, and maps of image scores by location.

Differences from the original study: (1) the paper used open Mapillary images processed by its own pipeline; this template uses 71 Google Street View views (2016–2026) from random points in Amsterdam; (2) the original app switched category at random every five images, allowed swiping and let people rate as many images as they liked; here each category is a block of 10 images with buttons. The earlier version of this template showed 10 photographs cropped from the paper PDF.
author: Danish, Labib, Ricker & Helbich

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. My answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: adult_confirm
elements.title: I confirm that I am 18 years or older.

elements.name: walkability
elements.title: Walkability
elements.description: Does this place look like an easy and safe place for people to travel on foot or using a walking-equivalent mobility aid (e.g. wheelchair)? This might include factors such as the quality of sidewalks, pedestrian crossings, street connectivity, and access to public amenities.

elements.name: bikeability
elements.title: Bikeability
elements.description: Does this place look accessible, attractive, safe and convenient for cycling as a mode of general-purpose transportation, or cycling-equivalent mobility aid (e.g. mobility scooter)? This might include factors such as cycle lanes, tracks, and parking, as well as the overall design of streets, junctions and any visible surroundings.

elements.name: pleasantness
elements.title: Pleasantness
elements.description: Does this place look enjoyable or pleasing to the senses or emotions? This might include factors such as the aesthetics of the surroundings, the quality of the air and lighting, the soundscape, and the presence of other people or natural elements.

elements.name: greenness
elements.title: Greenness
elements.description: Rate the apparent amount of vegetation and greenery in a given environment. This encompasses the presence of trees, shrubs, plants, and other natural elements.

elements.name: safety
elements.title: Safety
elements.description: Does this place look like you would feel protected from harm or danger, in terms of personal safety and security? Do you believe that it is likely that you would feel safe here at all times of day or night? This might include the presence of elements such as lighting, good maintenance, presence of other people and natural surveillance.
